title: AI to Help with Tiles/Tilesets?
author: CanaldoLontra
selftext:
Hello guys, i have been with the question about if there's any AI that can help me create tiles for my game, i am not great at tileset, i really would like to know if some AI can help me doing pixel art tiles, like a building. 

I have been testing GPT 5.5 and its very powerful, more than i expected, but Dall-E that it uses to generate images, does not support doing clean pixels, neither with personalized GPTs that others used, it just tries to simulate pixel and blurs and make bilinear, even if i says it to sharpen or make clean pixels or low resolution. Im doing my game in RPG Maker XP.

Are there any AI that can make perfect pixels like that?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
There are methods of converting mixels to pixel perfect art. For best results though you need to have at least enough digital art knowledge to manually refine the final piece. Adobe Illustrator has a Make Pixel Perfect option. However you'll also want to understand how color palettes generally work with Pixel art games, and usually this means converting your images colors in production (though tonemaps at runtime can achieve something similar but can have less intended results). After making sure the colors align with your game you'd then want to manually fix the lines to properly detail the pixel art (usually at one or two stages during this process you'll have the pixels end up in places that don't feel right and will need adjustment.)

An image generator cannot do these things. But they are deterministic and most of it is automatable via standard image processing methods. You can even set up a ComfyUI workflow to just run images through it and get 90% of the way there outside of some manual adjustments for polish.

But the whole point of pixel art is the low barrier to entry. This is something you'll want to understand better if you're going to use Pixel Art in a game. Because it's going to be held to a higher standard and it will become immediately clear how much effort you put into making the pixel art look good. You should read up on guides for sizing pixel art, animating it, etc, and make sure you understand all of its nuances before trying to use it. It's a great medium, especially for someone without a lot of practice with linework, brush strokes, etc. But it does demand some technical knowledge.

comments.author: FyhostElli
comments.body:
I tell chatgpt to make me a bunch of tilesets at specific sizes/pixels and themes. I tell it not add gridlines, and try to keep everything the same size. Then I open the image with windows and crop out each individual tile all the same size. Then I downloaded tiled, a free tileset making program, and turn those individual tiles into my own tilesets.

This was before the latest chatgpt image update. It's tilesets we're always off slightly in size between tiles, or really inconsistent themes. I find that having it make a bunch of similar tilesets and then just cropping out the indivual ones I like that visually match the best together, then turning them into my own tilesets with all the same sizes has been a very easy way to drastically improve the tilesets.
